title: Binary Berlekamp-inverse annihilator energy bound
statement: For every integer ell >= 2, n equal to 2 ell + 1 or 2 ell + 2, and 1 <= d < ell, put k=n-d. Partition the monic constant-one binary polynomials of degree k into simultaneous cosets according to their coefficients above degree d and the coefficients of their inverses modulo x^(ell+1) above degree d. If b_(C,D) is the polynomial-Mobius sum in one simultaneous coset, then the sum of b_(C,D)^2 over all cosets is at most 2^k.

provenance.source: Axeyum gf2-lemire lane; annihilator-averaged combined Berlekamp-discriminant and inverse-additive phase

notes: The exact operation binary_berlekamp_annihilator_energy_report proves the finite orthogonality and shift-correlation identities and checks both endpoint windows through ell=9, but finite enumeration is not evidence for the quantified statement. The stronger constant-one version with right side 2^(k-1) is refuted at (ell,k,d)=(6,9,5): the exact signed energy is 309, comprising the proved squarefree diagonal Q_9=171 and off-diagonal contribution 138. The same controls also satisfy the local target b_(C,D)^2 <= 2d #bucket; if proved, it implies E<d 2^k and strict weighted-term bounds from d=210 at both ell=300 endpoints. The displayed sharper 2^k bound would start at d=207 and d=208. Both remain partial tail inputs, not proofs of the full endpoint Mobius-convolution bound, so the universal Lemire fact does not depend on this conjectured fact.
